title: fix: use DeepInfra for Qwen embeddings with Fireworks fallback
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Routes `qwen/qwen3-embedding-8b` through DeepInfra `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-8B`, with Fireworks `accounts/fireworks/models/qwen3-embedding-8b` as the hidden shared fallback.
- Sets `paidOnly: true`, keeps multiplier 1, both existing aliases, text input, 128–4096 dimensions and 40,960-token support. No Pollinations GPU. User input price drops from $0.10 to $0.01/M tokens; Fireworks costs $0.10/M and retains the primary quote.
- Preserves character-heavy inputs by falling back before DeepInfra's 131,072-character limit. Reuses the existing embedding client, response mapping and fallback loop.
- Verified 146 Gen and 541 Enter tests, typechecking, formatting, real gateway primary/forced-fallback requests, aliases, batching, base64, permissions, caching, long inputs, wallet debits and staging billing records. DeepInfra's billing API confirms the rate.
- Capacity: 192/192 DeepInfra requests succeeded at 192 RPM with 4K-token inputs; p50 8.9s, p95 34.3s. Fireworks still throttles under load; manual validation needed quota cooldowns. Production rollout pending.

Pricing: [DeepInfra](https://deepinfra.com/Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-8B), [Fireworks](https://fireworks.ai/models/fireworks/qwen3-embedding-8b).

gist.headline: A cheaper path through the garden
gist.blurb: Qwen embeddings take the DeepInfra path, with Fireworks waiting at the next fork. Long inputs still have somewhere to go.
gist.summary: Routes qwen/qwen3-embedding-8b through DeepInfra at $0.01 per million input tokens instead of $0.10, with a hidden Fireworks fallback for provider failures and inputs exceeding DeepInfra's 131,072-character limit.
gist.impact: DeepInfra requests get the lower input rate, while character-heavy inputs can fall back to Fireworks; the existing aliases, 128–4096 dimensions, and 40,960-token support remain.
